fatal_errors: The hypothesis addresses dislocation-mediated mechanical strength and Portevin–Le Chatelier behavior, not high-temperature protective-oxide formation or persistence.
It substitutes FCC Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni single crystals for the target as-cast dual-phase BCC/B2 AlCrCoFeNi alloy.
It omits oxygen activity, air-versus-vacuum exposure, selective Al/Cr oxidation, alumina/chromia scale formation, scale cracking or spallation, and subsurface Al depletion.
The proposed compression, strain-rate-jump, TEM, and DFT tests cannot discriminate the requested oxidation mechanism.
No supporting evidence relevant to oxidation above 900 °C is cited, and the falsification rule is generic rather than tied to protective-scale coherence or persistence.
explanation: The response appears to reconstruct an unrelated study of temperature-dependent CRSS in concentrated-alloy single crystals. None of the central target elements—AlCrCoFeNi oxidation during heating to 1100 °C, air versus low-p(O2) comparison, outward Al/Cr diffusion, duplex Al2O3/Cr2O3 scale growth, or Al-depletion-driven substrate transformation—are recovered. Although its mechanical experiments are detailed and could test its own claims, they are irrelevant to the stated oxidation question and therefore receive only minimal discriminability credit.
